---
title: "In my words"
subtitle: "A few questions people ask me"
---

### Where do you come from?

I am the son of Venezuelan and Colombian parents. I studied mathematics at Universidad Simón
Bolívar in Caracas, and I grew up between two cultures, which helps me understand people who
see things differently.

### How did you get from mathematics to health?

I spent about ten years applying mathematics to real problems. First in banking, measuring
credit risk and screening for money laundering. Then I moved to health: I did a master's in
biostatistics in Bogotá and worked as the biostatistician of a university hospital, through
the COVID-19 pandemic.

### What do you work on now?

Functional data from wearable devices. A wrist accelerometer records how a person moves,
minute by minute, for days. Each person gives a curve, not a number. I work on Bayesian methods
that can use the whole curve and still run fast, and I write them as R packages so that other
people can use them.

### Where do you see yourself in five years?

I want to see the impact of research in the world. Many methods are published and then not
used. I would like my methods to be used by practitioners, and I would like to apply good
methods, mine or someone else's, to real problems. That can be in academia or in a company that
builds wearable devices. Functional data is an active field, with a lot still to develop, and
that is what I want to keep doing.

### Who shaped you as a researcher?

My advisor, Dr. Alexander McLain. As I said in my
[USC profile](https://www.sc.edu/study/colleges_schools/public_health/about/news/2025/iampublichealth_olejua_bios.php):

> What I admire most about Dr. McLain is his remarkable ability to adapt to anyone at their level
> in order to help them complete their research. He possesses a unique talent for breaking down
> complex concepts, providing guidance that is tailored to individual needs, and fostering an
> environment where curiosity and intellectual growth thrive.

### And outside work?

I dance Kizomba, ride my bicycle, and go hiking with my wife and our dog.
